thread:
rachael: Quick flag: onboarding sample-app is creating duplicate orgs when auth refresh and retries happen. Repro with netem.
sam: Logs?
rachael: gist of it: original request has Idempotency-Key, retry after refresh doesn't. Server creates twice.
kevin: Sounds like JS retry path rebuilds req without outgoing headers. Python/Go keep headers.
rachael: Repro steps I used: 1) run sample-app create-org with 30 concurrent users 2) sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms 3) observe duplicates
sam: Fix idea: stash outgoing headers on req (req._meta.outgoingHeaders) and use them for retries. Also switch backoff to full jitter to avoid synchronized retries. Pseudo: function backoff(attempt){const base=Math.min(1000*2**attempt,16000);return Math.random()*base;}
kevin: Add unit test simulating mid-flight auth refresh asserts Idempotency-Key present on retried envelope. Also add e2e that runs sample-app under netem and asserts one org per flow.
rachael: I'll open a PR with header-stash + tests and update sample-app to attach explicit idempotency keys per create.
ci-bot: Note: flaky test sdk-js::onboarding-duplicates has been failing in CI runs. See https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/24100
kevin: Cool. After merge, we'll cut a patch and add a short onboarding README note with the netem repro so new hires don't misinterpret duplicates as platform bugs.
sam: Thanks team, small change should clear a lot of confusion. :thumbsup:
